reviews.author: copilot-pull-request-reviewer[bot]
reviews.body: ## Pull request overview This PR retires the `fixNFTokenReserve` amendment and removes the conditional code paths associated with it, making the buyer reserve enforcement behavior unconditional and updating NFT unit tests accordingly. **Changes:** - Retire the `NFTokenReserve` fix amendment in `features.macro`. - Make the reserve check in `NFTokenAcceptOffer::transferNFToken` unconditional (no longer gated by `fixNFTokenReserve`). - Simplify `NFToken_test.cpp` scenarios by removing the pre-/post-amendment branching and updating feature sets used by the tests. ### Reviewed changes Copilot reviewed 3 out of 3 changed files in this pull request and generated 8 comments. | File | Description | | ---- | ----------- | | `src/test/app/NFToken_test.cpp` | Removes amendment-gated test branches and updates feature sets to reflect the retired fix. | | `src/libxrpl/tx/transactors/nft/NFTokenAcceptOffer.cpp` | Removes `fixNFTokenReserve` gating so buyer reserve checks always apply when owner count increases. | | `include/xrpl/protocol/detail/features.macro` | Moves `NFTokenReserve` from active fixes to the retired fixes list. | --- 💡 Add Copilot custom instructions for smarter, more guided reviews. Learn how to get started.

## High Level Overview of Change
Add checks in the NFTokenAcceptOffer transactor to check if OwnerCount changed, if it did, then check for the reserve requirement.


### Context of Change
Fixes a problem where someone could accept an NFT sell offer without needing reserve.

This problem, however, does not occur when buy offer is involved or in brokered mode.


### Type of Change



- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)
- [ ] New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality)
- [ ] Breaking change (fix or feature that would cause existing functionality to not work as expected)
- [ ] Refactor (non-breaking change that only restructures code)
- [x] Tests (You added tests for code that already exists, or your new feature included in this PR)
- [ ] Documentation Updates
- [ ] Release

reviewCommentsList.author: ckeshava
reviewCommentsList.body: Why are we verifying unit tests without the old fixes? We expect the validators to have pulled the latest code updates right? I was of the understanding that they would be Amendment Blocked otherwise.

reviewCommentsList.author: ckeshava
reviewCommentsList.body:
I don't understand why the reserve requirement must be a few drops higher, given that the transaction fees has already been paid.

According to the code, even if `buyerBalance == reserve` (line 350), the transaction is valid right?

reviewCommentsList.author: ckeshava
reviewCommentsList.body:
shouldn't Bob have at least `incReserve + drops(10) /* current transaction fee */ + drops(10) /* fees lost due to the previous transaction*/` ?

I don't understand why this is different from testcase in line 6888 ?

reviewCommentsList.author: scottschurr
reviewCommentsList.body:
We verify the behavior of unit tests with and without new amendments because we...

1. Don't know when (or if) the amendment will be approved.  We don't want to damage existing behavior while adding an amendment.
2. We like for the current version of rippled to process ledgers that are at least a couple of years old.  This is very helpful for ledger replay.  So we want to verify that the unit tests show old behavior when recent amendments are not enabled.

Hopefully that explanation makes some sense.

reviewCommentsList.author: ckeshava
reviewCommentsList.body: thanks for the explanation! I forgot about the amendment voting process :) 👍

reviewCommentsList.author: ckeshava
shawnxie999
shawnxie999
reviewCommentsList.body:
> I don't understand why this is different from testcase in line 6888 ?

The test case in line 68888 is testing the precise reserve requirements in the unit of drops. While in this test, it is exercising the behavior when Bob accepts many NFTs.

> shouldn't Bob have at least incReserve + drops(10) /* current transaction fee */ + drops(10) /* fees lost due to the previous transaction*/ ?

In this test case, Bob is funded with acctReserve + XRP(1). 1 XRP is more than enough for the transaction fees needed in this unit test. So we only need to worry about the incremental reserve that are taken up. Note that in unit test, the incremental reserve for an object is 50XRP, while the transaction fee is only 0.00001XRP

reviewCommentsList.body: Okay, I understand that. I was confused by the wording "... meaning that the reserve requirement is a few drops higher". Apart from this, I had the same understanding 👍

reviewCommentsList.author: ckeshava
reviewCommentsList.body: ah okay, I missed the fact that Bob has 1 XRP funds 👍
